`root>high` is what the viewer sees in the overlap. Although `root>low>inner` declares z-index 999, that value only has meaning *within* the stacking context created by its ancestor `root>low` (z-index 1). Stacking contexts are compared as whole units at the level where they're established, so `root>high` (z-index 2) competes directly against `root>low` (z-index 1) — not against `root>low>inner`'s 999. Since 2 > 1, the entire `root>low` subtree, including its inner div, paints below `root>high`. The report confirms this: "that whole context paints below root>high."

ANSWER: root>high
